Definition: the lip (as a natural boundary); by implication, language; by analogy, a margin (of a vessel, water, cloth, etc.)
BiblicalUsage: The word sâphâh means the lip (as a natural boundary); by implication, language; by analogy, a margin (of a vessel, water, cloth. In 1 Kings 4:29, we read, "…God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much…"; in 1 Samuel 1:13, "…heart; only her lips moved, but her voice…". You hear it again in 2 Chronicles 4:2 — "…a molten sea of ten cubits from brim…" — and in 2 Kings 2:13, "…up also the mantle of Elijah that fell…".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sâphâh matters because God chose this word, and it tells the truth about how God deals with his people. And I believe sâphâh still speaks to us today, because God's word does not go out of date.
